articles.title: Liverpool 1-1 Chelsea (6-5 on pens): Wesley Fofana misses crucial spot kick as Reds advance in Carabao Cup
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Liverpool beat Chelsea 6-5 on penalties after a 1-1 draw in normal time to reach the Carabao Cup last eight; Morgan Rogers and Cody Gakpo scored the goals from the spot before an even tie went to a shoot-out
articles.body:
Fofana, whose handball had gifted Liverpool their equaliser from the spot in normal time, scooped his penalty into the Kop after Giorgi Mamardashvili had denied Chelsea debutant Emmanuel Emegha.

Valentin Barco, another Chelsea substitute, also missed his spot kick, sending his effort against the post, but Ryan Gravenberch was thwarted by Mike Penders and Kostas Tsimikas fired over to keep a dramatic shoot-out going before Fofana's miss.

The goals also came from the spot in normal time, with Morgan Rogers and Cody Gakpo converting within three minutes of each other as a cagey first half burst into life before the break.

Both penalties were needlessly conceded, with Gravenberch first fouling Moises Caicedo when he was running away from goal, and Fofana then bizarrely raising his hand to touch a Tzimikas corner.

There were chances for both sides to win it in the second half, with Penders saving from substitute Bradley Barcola and Ronald Araujo, and Mamardashvili denying Rogers and Chelsea substitute Marco Palestra. But the two sides could not be separated.

While Chelsea named a strong starting line-up, Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola included four youngsters in Trey Nyoni, Rio Ngumoha, James McConnell and Lewis Koumas. But the Blues were unable to make their greater experience count.

The victory makes it five in a row in all competitions for Liverpool. For Chelsea, it's a second consecutive defeat after their Premier League loss to Spurs. The Blues also lost defender Maxence Lacroix to an apparent hamstring injury in the first half.

articles.title: Nico Williams agradece a Nahuel su 'asistencia' en el gol de Ferran: "Si no me empuja no llego ni en mil vidas"
articles.standfirst: El jugador del Athletic recuerda su pase en la final del Mundial
articles.summary: El jugador del Athletic recuerda su pase en la final del Mundial
articles.body: Nico Williams tiene una foto para toda la vida. Su asistencia con la cabeza, el pase atrás para que Ferran Torres pudiera hacer el gol de la victoria en la final del Mundial, ha quedado en la memoria y en la videoteca de todos los aficionados al fútbol. Pero hay un protagonista más en esta historia. "¿Sabes qué pasa? Es que esta es mortal... Creo que la gente no se ha dado cuenta pero... si no me llega a empujar, no llego", dice Nico Williams en una charla con Futbolemotion, recordando el empujón de Nahuel Molina cuando se encontraba dentro del área buscando el balón centrado por Pedro Porro. Y riéndose, dice: "No llego ni en mil vidas, que no llego". Recordando la acción, el extremo del Athletic cuenta su visión de la jugada: "Está el balón cayendo y me empuja, me choca así un poco con los dos brazos. Cuando venía el balón dije 'no llego' y cuando me empujó digo 'hostia', ahora llego". "No me da tiempo a rematar a puerta y digo, pues la dejo ahí y justo estaba Ferran", finaliza Williams.

articles.title: Arsenal Women 3-0 Benfica Women: Alessia Russo scores Women's Champions League hat-trick as Gunners win back-to-back games
articles.summary: Match report as Alessia Russo scores a hat-trick as Arsenal beat Benfica in the Women's Champions League league phase; she is now the highest-ever English goalscorer in the competition, overtaking Fran Kirby; the Gunners have won back-to-back games for the first time this season
articles.body:
The Gunners No 9 matched Fran Kirby's record (21) with her first-half opener - a low, diagonal effort that beat goalkeeper Lena Pauels.

Her next - a glancing header from Steph Catley's corner - made her the outright record holder, before adding another from the penalty spot after Caitlin Foord was fouled by Catarina Amado, taking her to 23 goals.

Russo scored the hat-trick in front of England boss Sarina Wiegman - who would also have been impressed by Georgia Stanway.

Perhaps the only blemish on Russo's otherwise brilliant evening was being flagged offside in the build-up to Foord's late fourth, which was ruled out.

The striker's own form mirrors that of Arsenal, who have won back-to-back games for the first time this season, alleviating the pressure after another poor start.

The result sends them second in the Champions League table - with their next European fixture a huge game at Barcelona on November 12, who they beat to win the title in 2025.

Russo: The derby win would've meant nothing without a win here

Arsenal hat-trick goalscorer Alessia Russo speaking to Disney+:

"It feels really nice. I love playing in the Champions League, especially with Arsenal with what we're building.

"The win was really important after building some momentum against Spurs. It's always loud here at Borehamwood, we love playing here and an important three points.

"We said that the North London derby wouldn't have meant anything if we didn't back it up tonight, so it was really important. Now hopefully we can build going forward.

"You could see how many shots on target we had. We've been really building, focusing on people feeling confident on stepping up and shooting from outside the box.

"Their 'keeper made some great saves and on another night, it might have been even more so a great performance."

articles.title: Iraola le gana el pulso a un Xabi Alonso al que se le sigue resistiendo Anfield
articles.standfirst: El lanzamiento de Wesley Fofana a las nubes condenó al conjunto 'blue' y dio el pase a cuartos al Liverpool
articles.summary: El lanzamiento de Wesley Fofana a las nubes condenó al conjunto 'blue' y dio el pase a cuartos al Liverpool
articles.body: No fueron pocas las noches de gloria que vivió Xabi Alonso como jugador del Liverpool entre 2004 y 2009. Como entrenador, sin embargo, la suerte en Anfield le sigue siendo esquiva. Cayó en dos ocasiones en Champions con el Real Madrid... y perdió el pulso con Iraola en la tanda de penaltis. Los 'reds' avanzan a cuartos de la Carabao. Asentado como lateral derecho, Iraola reclamó servicios de Ronaldo Araújo como central para acompañar a un Virgil Van Dijk que nunca descansa. Junto a Grevenberch y Gakpo, los únicos habituales en un Liverpool donde Mamardashvili ocupó la portería. Xabi Alonso fue todavía más 'radical': Malo Gusto ejerció como carril a pie cambiado; plantó un 'trivote' en el centro del campo; y, ante las críticas recibidas, ubicó a Welbeck como '9' por la baja de Joao Pedro. El Liverpool saltó con la autoridad que le otorgan sus últimos resultados desde la derrota contra el Manchester City. Plantó la línea de centrales a la altura del centro de campo y se hizo dueño y señor del balón. Les faltó, sin embargo, bastante mordiente a la hora de probar a un Mike Penders que no tuvo trabajo en toda la primera parte. Sólo Ngumoha, criado en la cantera 'blue', parecía proponer algo diferente. No sufrió el Chelsea... pero tampoco lograba amenazar al contragolpe. Ahora bien, la primera vez que pisaron área rival, Rogers reclamó un penalti inexistente de Araújo. A la siguiente, en el 37', Gravenberch sí 'barrió' dentro del área a Caicedo. Henderson, en su vuelta a Anfield, parecía dispuesto a ejecutarlo. Finalmente, sin embargo, se lo cedió a un Morgan Rogers que puso el balón en la escuadra. El 'accidente' por parte del canterano del Ajax, que ya salió señalado por su expulsión ante el Manchester City, fue bastante grosero. No tanto, eso sí, como el de un Wesley Fofana que, a escasos minutos del descanso, sacó una mano a pasear en la defensa de un saque de esquina. Un 'regalo' que Gakpo no desaprovechó. No fue el único 'palo' que se llevó el Chelsea antes de poner rumbo a vestuarios. Lacroix se rompió y Colwill tuvo que entrar en su lugar. Trató de sacarle rédito en Liverpool que, con la entrada de Barcola y Wirtz antes del 60', comenzó a imprimirle otra velocidad al partido. Se reivindicó Penders, con dos grandes intervenciones a Araújo y el propio Barcola, tras su grosero error contra el Tottenham el pasado fin de semana. El Chelsea necesitaba piernas frescas y, poco después, Xabi Alonso metió de una tacada a Palestra, Barco y el debutante Emegha. En el 78', Mamardashvili se agrandó para negarle el gol al italiano. El Chelsea, sin embargo, se sostuvo en la recta final con un doble bloqueo de Colwill y Acheampong a Wirtz y Barcola en boca de gol para llevar el partido a la tanda. El fallo del 'Colo' Barco en el cuarto penalti dejó al Chelsea contra las cuerdas. Tsimikas, sin embargo, también mandó su golpeo fuera. La parada de Penders a Gravenberch le daba a los 'blues' la oportunidad de sentenciar... pero Mamardashvili también frustró a Emegha. Quien no falló fue Joao Gómez. Trasladó toda la presión a Wesley Fofana y, después de su 'patinazo' en el 1-1 del Liverpool, mandó el balón a las nubes y condenó a los de Xabi Alonso después de 16 lanzamientos.

articles.title: Why Seahawks swapped practice squad tight ends after blockbuster trade
articles.summary: Factoring in the Quenton Nelson blockbuster, this looks like an intentional change in direction — not just an eye-for-an-eye swap.
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks added tight end Ben Sims to their practice squad Tuesday afternoon after releasing another tight end, Josiah Deguara, earlier that day. When comparing the two players and factoring in their blockbuster deal for Quenton Nelson, this looks like an intentional change in direction — not just the eye-for-an-eye swap it may seem on the surface.

Deguara was a fullback in college, but was able to convince the Green Bay Packers to use a third-round pick on him in 2020 with the hopes he could succeed in the "H-Back" role that lives between a tight end and a fullback. Examples of this working in the NFL include Zach Miller for the Seahawks, the late Aaron Hernandez for the New England Patriots, and Chris Cooley for the Washington Redskins . Where Deguara's pre-draft testing showed an 85th percentile athlete at fullback, the same numbers ranked in just the 66th percentile at tight end. He overcame this by being a willing blocker and a seemingly natural route runner at 242 pounds. He was also on a good team at the University of Cincinnati, which didn't hurt.

Sims is a different beast entirely. He's a natural receiving threat at tight end, standing over 6-foot-4 and recording 90th percentile times in the 40-yard dash and the 10- and 20-yard splits. He also had a 91st percentile broad jump and an 89.9th percentile vertical jump. He mirrors recently injured tight end Elijah Arroyo's profile as well as any option you could expect to find on waivers.

Deguara seemed like a desperate ploy to get more blockers on the field, when Seattle needed to improve their run game at all costs just a week ago . Since then, running back Emanuel Wilson became their first 100-yard rusher of the season on Sunday Night Football, Arroyo underwent season-ending surgery , and the Seahawks traded two draft picks to the Indianapolis Colts for a future Pro Football Hall of Fame guard in Nelson to further solidify their rushing attack. As the Seahawks look to replace Arroyo's profile with a size-and-speed receiving threat at tight end, Sims is the ideal prototype. Sims shouldn't be expected to provide the sheer route-running talent Arroyo had, but possesses the two most important traits to be effective in that role.

articles.title: Liverpool edge out Chelsea with penalty shootout victory in Carabao Cup
articles.summary: Liverpool 1-1 Chelsea (6-5 on penalties): Wesley Fofana’s wayward spot-kick sent the Reds into the league cup quarter-finals
articles.body:
When Xabi Alonso was a Liverpool player, he won the Champions League and the FA Cup, both on penalties. He scored in a penalty shootout in the 2007 Champions League semi-finals to help eliminate Chelsea .

As he returned to Anfield, on a quest for further silverware, perhaps it was inevitable it would all end in penalties. Perhaps it was inevitable, too, that it would end with a defeat for Chelsea. They have had five shootouts against Liverpool and lost them all.

So, when Wesley Fofana dispatched his penalty into the Kop, there was a certain familiarity for them. It compounded a bad night for the French defender, who had conceded a first-half spot kick, too. For Alonso, managing Chelsea in a rare season when they are not in Europe, a chance of a trophy has escaped his grasp.

For Liverpool, the penalty that proved decisive came from a man who, in a decade in their defence, has never scored in regulation time in a match, in Joe Gomez. There were some terrific spot kicks, with Alexis Mac Allister, Alexander Isak , Cody Gakpo, Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola also scoring.

After Valentin Barco hit the post, Kostas Tsimikas, who had scored the winning penalty in the 2022 FA Cup final shootout, had the chance to repeat the feat, but skied his shot into the Kop. It was in effect sudden death when Jordan Henderson held his nerve amid jeers from the Liverpool fans who used to celebrate him.

There had been no saves in the first 12 penalties, then two in two, Mike Penders parrying Ryan Gravenberch's effort and Giorgi Mamardashvili stopping from Emmanuel Emegha. As the drama was backloaded, Liverpool prevailed. For the third time in six seasons, they knocked out Chelsea.

But spot kicks were a theme of the night. The only goals came from 12 yards as they traded penalties in the space of a few minutes, both conceded stupidly and needlessly.

Ryan Gravenberch had ploughed through Moises Caicedo and Morgan Rogers converted the penalty; he probably owed his presence on spot-kick duties to Cole Palmer's ban, after his sending off against Tottenham but then Gakpo, too, is normally further down the queue to take them.

But he drilled in his spot kick after Fofana handled the ball in his attempts to stop Virgil van Dijk from meeting Tsimikas' corner. No sooner had Chelsea been gifted a lead than they presented Liverpool with a leveller.

There could have been a winner thereafter. After his traumatic outing against Tottenham, Mike Penders made a brilliant save to repel Ronald Araujo's header. It was redemptive, too, when he denied Barcola, the rookie showing his considerable talent.

At the other end, Mamardashvili denied Marco Palestra a first Chelsea goal when the summer signing was supplied by Rogers. Over the 90 minutes, the scoreline was probably fair. One element of it was welcome for Alonso.

It was his third game at Anfield as a manager, and for three different clubs. He finally saw one of his sides score, though only after they cancelled each other out.

Alonso can be flexible in his tactics and sought to match up his boyhood friend Iraola's system. His Chelsea played 4-4-1-1; so, two decades ago, did Rafa Benitez's Liverpool teams. There were echoes of the past, some of the rancour of the clashes of the 2000s. When the Anfield crowd saluted one of the heroes of 2005, a Spaniard signed by Rafa Benitez, they were singing about Luis Garcia, not Alonso.

Another of Liverpool's finest midfielders of the 21st century, Henderson, was greeted with boos on his return to Anfield, largely for joining Chelsea; he received a friendlier reception when he came back with Brentford in May. If his move to Stamford Bridge was a surprise, so was his deployment here, in an unexpectedly advanced role as a No 10. Perhaps it made him the deputy for the suspended Palmer. His Liverpool counterpart was James McConnell, another holding midfielder playing just behind a lone striker.

With more defensively-minded personnel in attacking areas, perhaps it was unsurprising there were few chances early on. There was a shortage of creativity, a surfeit of caution. The swift exchange of goals came from mistakes. The first shot of note in open play came from Gakpo, a couple of minutes before half-time. Penders parried it.

The absentees were a reason for that lack of attacking threat. With Joao Pedro injured and Palmer out, Chelsea only had one of their first-choice front three. Liverpool kept their three biggest buys in reserve, three £100m players on a bench that cost more than half a billion pounds. Yet each side could have benefited from more quality on the pitch.

Having held his big buys back, Iraola turned to Barcola and Wirtz for the last half-hour. The German, so good for Alonso at Bayer Leverkusen, scored his spot kick. And in a marathon shootout, Chelsea missed three of theirs.
